claim: disrobe re-hosts Dalvik method bodies into class bytecode that the real JVM bytecode verifier accepts under -Xverify:all, on the committed dex corpus.
detail: 118 of 118 VERIFIER-PRESENTED classes in the committed EdgeCases/EdgeCasesKt/Hello dex pass the real JVM bytecode verifier (-Xverify:all) with 0 lifter verify failures, so the plotted figure is the verifier-presented ratio. State the other denominator too: the corpus holds 155 classes and 37 of them are link-skipped, never reaching the verifier because they reference supertypes the harness does not bundle, Kotlin's Function1 among them. That is a harness limit rather than a lifter defect, but it means 118 of 155 classes are verifier-attested and the remaining 37 are ungraded, not passing. A live-range-splitting pass recovers bodies with conflicting register types across joins, and 317 re-hosted method bodies verify clean with 0 failures, every non-stub recovered body re-hosted into an Object carrier and run through -Xverify:all. Floor 118 classes; the reference is the JVM rejecting malformed bytecode, not the lifter's own report.
gate_source: crates/disrobe-pass-jvm/tests/dalvik_verifier_gate.rs (COMMITTED_VERIFY_CLEAN_CLASSES 118, COMMITTED_LIFTER_VERIFY_FAILURES 0, COMMITTED_CORPUS_CLASSES 155, COMMITTED_BODY_VERIFY_CLEAN 317, COMMITTED_BODY_VERIFY_FAILURES 0, every one an equality rather than a floor); reference = -Xverify:all over assemble_jar output, not the lifter self-report; measured 118 of 118 verifier-presented classes with 37 link-skipped and 317 re-hosted bodies clean on JDK 25, and because the corpus is committed and the translation deterministic, a figure that moves either way fails this gate until the documents state the new one

oracle.external: real JVM verifier (-Xverify:all over the assembled jar; the JVM rejects malformed bytecode)

title: Dalvik recovered bodies, real JVM verifier
